criteria.quote: Golbat bit the wrong Pokémon and lost some teeth.
criteria.revision: Replace it with: "Hunger can drive Golbat to bite a Steel-type Pokémon—and leave it missing some of its own fangs."

criteria.quote: Its fangs are hollow like straws, making them unexpectedly fragile.
What kind of bite can make Golbat lose its own fangs?
criteria.revision: Change the open loop to: "What happens when hunger drives Golbat to bite a Steel-type Pokémon?" Then delay the answer until the missing-fangs scene.

criteria.quote: Golbat bit the wrong Pokémon and lost some teeth.
criteria.revision: Reorder the story so it moves from hollow, unexpectedly fragile fangs, to hunger driving Golbat toward a Steel-type, to the reveal that it can end up missing some fangs. Remove the opening consequence so the stakes build instead of arriving first.

criteria.quote: Its fangs are hollow like straws, making them unexpectedly fragile.
criteria.revision: Move the missing-fangs reveal after the hollow-fangs and Steel-type scenes, so the audience first learns why the fangs are fragile and only then learns what hunger can make Golbat bite.

criteria.quote: That bite can leave Golbat missing some of its fangs.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated "fragile tools" scene with: "Golbat can drink more than 10 ounces of blood in one go—and too much can leave it unable to fly." This adds a distinct feeding consequence supported by the research.

criteria.quote: Golbat's hollow blood-sucking fangs are powerful, but biting Steel can cost it some teeth.
criteria.revision: Replace it with: "Golbat's fangs are hollow and specialized for sucking blood, but hunger can drive it to bite a Steel-type Pokémon and leave it missing some fangs." Remove "powerful," which the research does not establish.

criteria.quote: Cool weakness or terrible design choice?
criteria.revision: Replace it with: "Does Golbat's hollow, fragile fang design make it perfectly specialized for blood—or vulnerable when hunger drives it to bite Steel?"
